notes: בֶּן־שְׁנָתוֹ is split rather than fused: the ASV spends old on the construct and a year on the rectum, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet and rule 2 splits it; leaving בֶּן unrepresented to hand its word to the rectum is what rule 19 forbids. The suffix is unrepresented because the ASV writes no possessive in a year old.

The temporal בְּ before the infinitive construct takes when and the infinitive keeps are fulfilled (rule 52); the second בֶן־יוֹנָה is rendered attributively as young pigeon, following the ASV rather than imposing of (rule 28).

תֹר → a turtle dove is headed on dove under rule 31's tie clause, reading dove as the class noun and turtle as the ASV's specifier; the competing head on turtle, which carries the species lexeme under rule 31's primary subtraction test, is named in that unit's note (rule 8). The same tie is resolved the same way at LEV.12.8, but each was decided on its own evidence.

עֹלָה and חַטָּאת head on burnt and sin, which is the reading rule 31 states for עֹלָה itself; the three-term chain פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד carries supplied the's on the two construct levels (rules 19, 29).
